---
title: "mask_utils"
---

## Overview

`mask_utils.hpp` provides mask raster helpers: sparse `Mask2D` ↔ dense `Image`,
nearest-neighbor resize between canvas sizes, and batch binary processing.

**Header:** `src/DataObjects/Masks/utils/mask_utils.hpp`  
**Tests:** `src/DataObjects/Masks/utils/mask_utils.test.cpp`

## Spatial conventions

Only **resize** functions carry a grid convention. Placement helpers
(`mask_to_binary_image`, `binary_image_to_mask`) write/read integer indices
without resampling.

### Pixel-center (canonical target)

Used by `map_dest_to_source`, `resize_mask`, `TensorToMask2D`, PyTorch
`ImageEncoder`, and OpenCV `cv2.resize` sampling.

Continuous image → tensor coordinate (one axis):

```
t = (x + 0.5) * T / I - 0.5
```

Inverse NN when expanding a mask raster (destination pixel `d` samples source `s`):

```
s = floor((d + 0.5) * S / D - 0.5)   // clamped; Phase 1 may switch to round at half-integers
```

### Edge-aligned (legacy — not supported for new code)

Previously used by `Mask2DEncoder` (`round(x * T/I)`) and some training point
transforms (`x * out_w / in_w`). Corner `0→0`, `W-1→out_w-1`.

```
t = round(x * T / I)
```

This is **not** paired with `map_dest_to_source` and causes 1–2 px shifts at
640×480 → 256×256. Do not add a second public `resize_mask_*` API for this;
compare conventions in unit tests only.

### Comparison at 640×480 → 256 (width axis)

| Image `x` | Pixel-center `map_dest_to_source(x,256,640)` | Edge-aligned `round(x*256/640)` |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 297 | 118 | 119 |
| 301 | 120 | 120 |
| 228 | 90 | 91 |
| 209 | 83 | 84 |
| 281 | 112 | 112 |

Rows where the two columns differ by 1 are exactly the half-integer boundary
cases in continuous space.

## Functions

| Function | Resize? | Convention |
|---|---|---|
| `map_dest_to_source` | Yes (1D index map) | Pixel-center inverse NN |
| `resize_mask` | Yes | Pixel-center inverse NN on binary raster |
| `mask_to_binary_image` | No | N/A |
| `binary_image_to_mask` | No | N/A |
| `apply_binary_image_algorithm` | No | Uses canvas size as-is |
